newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Owner wants Swedish banks to resume talks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Owner wants Swedish banks to resume talks - paper.

text.p: A major shareholder in both state-controlled Swedish bank Nordbanken and Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken wants the two banks to resume merger talks, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

"I regret the two banks did not proceed farther in their discussions and I would welcome them resuming talks," said Bo Eklof, managing director of Swedish insurance company SPP, quoted by financial daily Finanstidningen.
A merger between the two banks would result in significant synergies on the cost side, Eklof told the newspaper. He said the most favourable mergers were those between banks, the newspaper said.
Market rumours that the two banks would merge drove up share prices in S-E-Banken and Nordbanken sharply since last autumn.
The two banks surprised the market on February 3 by announcing that merger talks between them had ended with no conclusion.
"To merge insurance companies is less favourable, while a merger between a bank and an insurance company is the most difficult to bring about," Eklof said.
Swedish banks are relatively small compared to others in European Union member countries, and for that reason a merger between the two would be good, Eklof said.
